claim: There is no positive exponential relative-entropy decay exponent uniform over all collision frequencies nu>0 and torus lengths ell>0 for the unit-temperature kinetic Fokker-Planck equation, even if the finite multiplicative prefactor may depend on nu and ell.
quantifiers: For every d>=1, nu>0, ell>0, and every all-state bound H(F_t|M)<=C(nu,ell) exp(-lambda(nu,ell)t) H(F_0|M) with finite C, lambda<=2 min{nu,(2pi/ell)^2/nu}.
assumptions: Periodic domain T^d_ell, standard Gaussian M(v)=(2pi)^(-d/2) exp(-|v|^2/2).
Forward equation d_t F+v.grad_x F=nu div_v(grad_v F+vF).
Relative entropy is with respect to normalized dx times M(v)dv; initial states are probability densities with finite entropy.
The claimed inequality is required for every admissible initial density and all t>=0; its prefactor is finite for each parameter pair.
proof: For k=2pi/ell, phi=cos(k x_1-k v_1/nu) is bounded, mean zero, and direct differentiation gives G_nu phi=-(k^2/nu)phi. Thus F_t=M(1+epsilon exp(-k^2 t/nu)phi), 0<epsilon<1, is a positive probability solution. Its KL entropy equals J(epsilon exp(-k^2 t/nu)), where J(a)=(2pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2pi)(1+a cos theta)log(1+a cos theta)dtheta=a^2/4+O(a^4). Its asymptotic exponent is exactly 2k^2/nu, forcing lambda<=2k^2/nu. For the other constraint, linearize any all-state KL inequality at M using bounded mean-zero velocity perturbations; density extends the resulting L2 semigroup estimate to h=v_1, for which exp(tG_nu)h=exp(-nu t)h. Hence lambda<=2nu. Together these give the stated bound and refute a common positive rate as ell->infinity, nu->0, or nu->infinity.

costs.representation: One spatial Fourier mode and one velocity coordinate; O(1) exact symbolic operations.

baseline: The exact fixed-parameter mode is compared with the established DMS/ADSW quadratic L2 hypocoercivity bounds. These do not imply a nonlinear KL lower bound.
falsifier: Substitute phi into G_nu and verify the residual; or compute the positive KL solution above and compare its asymptotic exponent with any proposed lambda.

claim: For fixed nu>0 and ell>0, the linear kinetic Fokker-Planck semigroup on T^d_ell has an explicit exponential quadratic-L2 estimate with exponent lambda_DMS=(1/12)nu k_*^2/(nu^2+k_*^2), k_*=2pi/ell.
quantifiers: For d>=1, every mean-zero initial perturbation F_0 in L2(dx M^(-1)dv), all t>=0, and the equation and equilibrium in KFP-UNIFORM-RATE-OBSTRUCTION, ||F_t-F_infty||^2<=3 exp(-lambda_DMS t)||F_0-F_infty||^2.
assumptions: Same periodic unit-temperature Gaussian KFP model as the first claim.
The claim concerns quadratic L2 entropy only; it does not assert a global nonlinear KL inequality.
proof: Use the primary-source DMS modewise bound for unit collision rate: ||Fhat(t,xi)||^2<=3 exp[-(1/12)|xi|^2/(1+|xi|^2)t]||Fhat_0(xi)||^2, with Gaussian constants Theta=1, K=3, theta=kappa=1. Rescale time s=nu t; the effective Fourier parameter is eta=xi/nu. Thus the squared-norm exponent in physical time is (1/12)nu|xi|^2/(nu^2+|xi|^2). On T^d_ell the least nonzero frequency is k_*=2pi/ell. The zero spatial mode is purely microscopic and has squared-norm rate 2nu, larger than the displayed nonzero-mode rate. Parseval gives the stated estimate.

modified_entropy.operator: A_eta=(I+(T_eta Pi)^*T_eta Pi)^(-1)(T_eta Pi)^*, T_eta F=i(v dot eta)F, Pi F=M integral F dv
modified_entropy.mode_formula: A_eta F=-i M (eta dot integral v F(v)dv)/(1+|eta|^2)
modified_entropy.scope: Quadratic L2 modification, not full nonlinear relative entropy.

macro_micro.microcoercivity: -<L0F,F>=integral M|grad_v(F/M)|^2 >= ||(I-Pi)F||^2 by the unit Gaussian Poincare inequality.
macro_micro.macrocoercivity: ||T_eta Pi F||^2=|eta|^2||Pi F||^2 for each Fourier mode.
macro_micro.commutator: [grad_v,j, v dot grad_x]=grad_x,j; in rescaled time the transport commutator is nu^(-1)grad_x,j.
macro_micro.bounded_cross_terms: ADSW gives C_M(s)=s(1+sqrt(3)s)/(1+s^2), s=|eta|, with model-specific bounds for A T Q and A L0.
